What really happens when you type a URL into your browser?

📌 Introduction

Week 00 of the DevOps Micro Internship focused on understanding the fundamentals of the Internet and computer networking.

Before learning technologies such as Linux, Git, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS and CI/CD, it is important to understand what actually happens underneath the applications and tools we use every day.

My main question: What actually happens after I type a website address into my browser and press Enter?

🌍 What Happens When You Type a URL?

When we enter a URL such as https://example.com, many networking operations happen behind the scenes before the webpage appears.

Browser
↓
DNS Resolution
↓
TCP Connection
↓
TLS / HTTPS
↓
HTTP Request
↓
Web Server
↓
HTTP Response
↓
Browser renders webpage

🔎 1. DNS Resolution

Humans prefer domain names such as google.com, but computers communicate using IP addresses.

DNS, or Domain Name System, translates a domain name into the IP address associated with it.

Example:

Domain: example.com

↓ DNS lookup ↓

IP address: 93.184.216.34

This allows the browser to discover where the requested server is located on the network.

📡 2. TCP Connection

After discovering the server's IP address, the browser needs to establish a reliable connection with it.

For traditional HTTPS communication, TCP provides the underlying reliable transport connection.

🤝 TCP Three-Way Handshake

Client                 Server
```

SYN  -------------------->

```
   <--------------------  SYN + ACK
```

ACK  -------------------->
```

This handshake establishes the TCP connection between the client and server.

🔐 3. HTTPS & TLS

HTTPS protects communication between the browser and the web server by using TLS.

TLS provides important security properties such as encryption and server authentication.

Why HTTPS matters

  • 🔒 Protects data from being easily read in transit
  • 🪪 Helps authenticate the server
  • 🛡️ Helps detect tampering with communication

📨 4. HTTP Request

Once the connection is ready, the browser sends an HTTP request to the server. 

GET / HTTP/1.1
```

Host: example.com
User-Agent: Browser
Accept: text/html
```

The request tells the server what resource the client wants and provides additional information through HTTP headers.

📬 5. HTTP Response

The server processes the request and sends a response back to the browser. 

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

Content-Type: text/html


...
```

The status code 200 OK indicates that the request was successfully processed.

🧩 Important Networking Concepts

Concept Purpose
DNS Maps domain names to IP addresses
IP Provides addressing between networked devices
TCP Provides reliable transport
TLS Provides security for HTTPS communication
HTTP Defines web request and response communication
Server Processes requests and provides resources

🛠️ Practical Learning

During this assignment, I focused on understanding the relationship between different networking layers rather than treating the Internet as a black box.

Some useful commands and tools for exploring networking include: 

# Check DNS resolution
```

nslookup example.com

# Check connectivity

ping example.com

# Inspect HTTP communication

curl -I https://example.com

# Trace network path

traceroute example.com
```

🧠 What I Learned

  • A URL is only the starting point of a much larger networking process.
  • DNS converts human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
  • TCP provides reliable communication between systems.
  • HTTPS uses TLS to secure web communication.
  • HTTP defines how browsers and web servers communicate.
  • Understanding networking fundamentals makes DevOps concepts easier to understand.

🚀 Why This Matters for DevOps

Networking is one of the foundations of DevOps.

Later topics such as cloud computing, containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, load balancers, APIs and infrastructure as code all depend on networking concepts.

Understanding what happens underneath the application helps me troubleshoot systems instead of simply memorizing commands.

📚 Key Takeaways

  1. DNS helps locate the destination server.
  2. TCP establishes reliable communication.
  3. TLS protects HTTPS communication.
  4. HTTP defines the request/response process.
  5. The browser combines all of these steps to retrieve and display web content.

🎯 Conclusion

Week 00 gave me a clearer understanding of what happens behind a simple web request.

Something as simple as typing a URL into a browser involves DNS, IP addressing, transport protocols, encryption, HTTP communication and server-side processing.

This foundation will be useful as I continue my journey through Linux, Git, cloud computing, automation, containers, Kubernetes and DevOps.
